chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam and Ibn Mahbub, from Mu'awiya ibn Wahb who said:
The pigeon is from the birds of the Prophets (peace be upon them).

key_terms.الأنبياء عليهم السلام: The Prophets, peace be upon them — the messengers sent by God
key_terms.الحمام: Pigeon/dove — a bird traditionally kept by Muslims, especially in Arab culture
key_terms.طيور الأنبياء: Birds of the Prophets — birds associated with or kept by the prophets of God

ai.seo_question: Is keeping pigeons a prophetic tradition in Islam?
ai.summary: Mu'awiya ibn Wahb, a companion of Imam al-Sadiq (AS), reports that the pigeon is counted among the birds associated with the Prophets (peace be upon them all). This statement reflects the high esteem in which pigeons were held in early Islamic and prophetic culture, where keeping and caring for pigeons was considered a praiseworthy activity connected to prophetic tradition. The audience would have understood this as an endorsement of keeping pigeons as pets or for other lawful purposes.
